title: A Model of Growth through Creative Destruction
brief_synopsis: The paper presents an endogenous growth model where growth arises from vertical innovations that replace older technologies through creative destruction. Equilibrium is governed by a forward-looking difference equation in which current research effort falls when firms expect more research in the next period. It studies the properties of stationary equilibria, identifies conditions under which cyclical equilibria and no-growth traps can occur, and argues that equilibrium growth may be either above or below the social optimum because business-stealing offsets standard spillover and appropriability effects. The paper also concludes that innovations tend to be inefficiently small.
